items.transcript: Would you like to have a cup of coffee?
items.feedback: Listen for the short words: to have a cup of.

items.transcript: The little shop closes at six on Sundays.
items.feedback: Check the final sounds in closes and Sundays.

items.transcript: Please keep your ticket until the end of the trip.
items.feedback: Keep your ticket is the instruction; until tells you how long.

items.transcript: I've been trying to cut down on caffeine lately.
items.feedback: I've is a contraction. Cut down on means reduce how much you consume.

items.transcript: The flight has been delayed due to severe weather conditions.
items.feedback: Has been delayed is passive. Due to introduces the reason.

items.transcript: We haven't decided whether to move the meeting to Friday.
items.feedback: Keep the negative contraction haven't; whether introduces the decision.

items.transcript: Although public transport is convenient, it can become overcrowded during rush hour.
items.feedback: Although introduces a contrast. Check the spelling of overcrowded.

items.transcript: Governments should allocate more resources to improve access to higher education.
items.feedback: Allocate resources means decide how to use them. Listen for both occurrences of to.

items.transcript: Unless the proposal is revised, the committee is unlikely to approve it.
items.feedback: Unless gives a condition. Unlikely changes the meaning of the final clause.
